The natural reading is that /cases/pending does not serve per-case rows into the text excerpt_of can see - and if case identifiers are not reachable there, A RESPONDENT NAME PROBABLY IS NOT EITHER, and a false find on row 4 is close to UNINFORMATIVE ABOUT THE DOCKET. That is 0906-B6's defect - a literal unreachable by construction - and I am naming it in advance rather than discovering it in the vetting round. Row 4 is fired anyway because next step 2 directs it and because a FALSIFICATION there would be genuinely surprising and genuinely valuable; but its CONFIRMATION carries almost no weight and no seat may spend it as though it did. INSTRUMENT SEMANTICS, RE-READ FROM scripts/fetch_relay.py TODAY RATHER THAN CARRIED FROM MEMORY: excerpt_of deletes script and style blocks, then every remaining tag, then normalises whitespace, and searches the WHOLE resulting body case-insensitively; find_matched is true if and only if that search returns a non-empty window. A literal living only inside a script block, a style block or an HTML attribute is UNREACHABLE BY CONSTRUCTION and its absence proves nothing about the page. NOTE ALSO that the search is CASE-INSENSITIVE, so row 2 and row 4 will match 'netherlands' and 'NETHERLANDS' as well as 'Netherlands', and a confirmation is therefore a stronger null than a case-sensitive one would be. BINDING READING RULE ON ROWS 1-4: these are CHANNEL DIAGNOSTICS SERVING ONE NAMED THREAD, not discovery. STANDING READING RULES, restated because they are the ones this council keeps having to re-learn: a returned excerpt establishes what its own 400 characters contain and NOTHING about what lies outside them; an absent literal establishes that excerpt_of found no match on the returned body - A STATEMENT ABOUT THE FETCH, NOT ABOUT THE RESOURCE; a 404 or non-200 is information about the URL pattern, NEVER about the underlying matter; every count derived from this reduction carries its COMMIT as well as its scope (0903-B2); a denominator over a mutable register is enumerated or is stated as 'files present in the tree at <commit>' and never as 'committed' (0906-B10); and every byte count and sha256 held for a page is a statement about ONE RESPONSE, not about the page, and citations must say which - which is why the 2026-09-07 byte counts above are attributed to those two responses and not to those two pages.
